messages:
maria: Heads-up — our GPU Savings Plan for eu-west-1 is up for renewal next month (term end ~2026-04-20). Utilization looks uneven: A10g pools ~64% but p3/p4 footprints are shifting across regions. Need a quick decision on renew vs convert to convertible RIs or a mixed approach. Chart: https://s3.redwood-internal.com/billing/gpu-util-euw.pdf
ken: Are you including prefix/KV cache effects in that util calc? last time the agg job missed ~10% because of cache hits.
sam: I pulled a fast sample: committed-hour coverage ~68% across p4d/p3; effective usage after shared-pool adjustment ~58% for A10g. Converting family reduces some of the upside on p4d price.
maria: I used monthly-agg (billing/compute/savingsplan/agg). raw csv uploaded: s3://redwood-billing/eu-west1-agg-2026-02.csv — includes prefix cache column.
liam: Is moving some work to us-east-1 an option? we have spare reserved capacity there. Might save on commit cost but network egress and latency could bite.
sylvia: Compliance note: several EU customers require regional residency — we can't shift all production. Need a hybrid plan.
maria: Proposed options: 1) renew identical SP for eu-west-1 (1yr) — lowest ops overhead. 2) purchase convertible RIs (2yr) to allow family changes but slightly higher unit price. 3) partial renewal + rightsize nodes and use Dedicated burst for peaks. Anyone have quick pros/cons?
ken: +1 for running a 7-day simulated forecast mapping instance families to usage over the last 90 days. I'll run and share by EOD. Also quick CLI to enumerate active RIs: ```aws ec2 describe-reserved-instances --filters Name=state,Values=active --region eu-west-1```
billingbot: Automated summary uploaded: SavingsPlan eu-west-1 — committed_hours: 10800, used_hours: 7480, utilization: 69.3%, estimated additional savings if converted to convertible mix: ~12%. (report link: https://s3.redwood-internal.com/billing/reports/eu-west1-spsummary-2026-02.pdf)
sam: If we go convertible, my vote is mixed allocation: p4d 40%, a10g 40%, 20% flexible. That hedges model churn and new quantized variants.
liam: FYI spot eviction rates in eu-west-1 spiked last week — that pushed fallback to on-demand and spiked cost for some batch runs. If we commit more, we should also tighten scheduling to avoid on-demand fallbacks.
sylvia: From a product/contract side: can we limit the commit to 1 year so we can reassess next model cycle? Finance prefers 2yr discounts but product needs agility.
maria: Good points. Action items: @ken run the family-mapped forecast and post numbers, @sam assemble a convertible-mix P&L with cashflow impact, I'll draft recommendation for finance and legal. Let's reconvene after Ken's forecast. :memo:
